fair_value.method: Sum of the parts on 3.95B shares outstanding (10-Q: 3,949M at 2026-06-30; $1.47T market cap at $372.11), 12 months forward. Core auto+services ~30x 2027E consensus EPS $2.17 ex-energy (~$65/sh); energy ~$2B EBIT x 27 = ~$54B (~$14/sh); net cash $27.4B plus SpaceX stake ~$3-4B (~$8/sh); probability-weighted autonomy ~$520B (~$132/sh) and Optimus ~$260B (~$66/sh). Total ~$285. About 70% of it is option value, so it is a judgment anchor, not a floor.

methods.name: Sum of the parts (primary)
methods.detail: 65 (auto, 30x $2.17 ex-energy) + 14 (energy, $54B) + 8 (net cash $27.4B + SpaceX ~$3.5B) + 132 (autonomy $520B, down from $550B after the NHTSA Special Order and EU vote slip) + 66 (Optimus $260B), all on 3.95B shares.

methods.name: Forward P/E cross-check
methods.detail: 120x 2027E EPS $2.17. 120x is a generous premium multiple for a ~20%+ EPS grower with option value; 171x at spot.

methods.name: Analyst targets (evidence only)
methods.detail: 43 analysts: average $396.94, median $415; 19 Buy, 20 Hold, 4 Sell. Not used as the answer; it shows sell-side still pays for autonomy optionality above my SOTP.

bear.story: Capex >$25B keeps FCF near zero or negative; operating margin stays ~1-4%; Q3/Q4 deliveries miss (Goldman 435k vs ~461k consensus). NHTSA's Cybercab Special Order leads to a pause or an FMVSS exemption process (no foot brake). EU FSD approval stalls past December with only 7 of 27 states on board, and robotaxi stays at a few hundred cars in TX/FL. The multiple compresses toward ~100x ~$2 EPS plus reduced option value.

base.story: Revenue grows low-teens and 2027 EPS lands ~$2.2. Energy margins recover toward the mid-20s. NHTSA resolves with paperwork or a limited exemption and no fleet halt. Robotaxi expands to ~a dozen metros with a slow Cybercab ramp. EU vote happens in 1H27. The story multiple holds roughly and the stock ends near spot.

bull.story: Unsupervised FSD on customer cars or v15 is validated, the Cybercab fleet scales into the thousands with credible unit economics, Optimus external units ship and Semi volume ramps. An AI/SpaceX narrative re-rates the stock and it retakes the $499 high.

thesis_break_reason: About 15% below the July 2026 capitulation low ($297-304), which already priced a negative-FCF quarter and a 1.4% operating margin. A sustained trade near $255 would most likely mean the autonomy thesis broke rather than ordinary 46%-vol noise: NHTSA forcing a Cybercab halt or a lengthy exemption process, a serious robotaxi safety incident, or unsupervised expansion stalling. It could also mean core auto turning loss-making while debt-funded capex eats the ~$43B cash pile.

catalysts.event: Tesla's sworn response due on NHTSA Special Order (21 requests) on Cybercab FMVSS self-certification; follow-on NHTSA action possible in Q4
Q3 2026 production and deliveries (consensus ~461k; Goldman 435k, Barclays 475k)
Q3 2026 earnings: margins, capex path, FCF, debt facilities, Cybercab/Optimus updates
Earliest possible EU TCMV vote on EU-wide FSD Supervised (no vote on Oct 6; needs 15 states and 65% of population)
Musk target of robotaxi in ~12 states by year-end; FSD v15 release
Q4 2026 deliveries and FY26 earnings with 2027 capex guidance
Annual meeting; Optimus production disclosures; possible Tesla-SpaceX combination (~47% odds by May 2027 on prediction markets)

key_uncertainties: Outcome of NHTSA Special Order on Cybercab (no foot-controlled brake vs FMVSS 135): paperwork, exemption process, or forced pause
Pace and safety of robotaxi scaling beyond ~200 unsupervised vehicles in 7 TX/FL metros; FSD v15 timing
EU FSD approval timing (December at the earliest, only 7 of 27 states so far) and full China approval
Duration of negative or near-zero FCF from a $25B+ capex cycle, funded partly by up to $30B of debt capacity
Core auto margins (1.4% operating margin in Q2) and collapsing regulatory credits
Energy margin recovery after the Q2 warranty charge
Tesla-SpaceX merger: two-sided and uncertain (prediction markets ~47% by May 2027)
Dilution from the 423.7M-share 2025 CEO performance award as market-cap milestones are hit
reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor's corrections all point slightly lower, and I verified the important one: the share count is 3.95B (10-Q shows 3,949M at June 30, up from 3,751M at year-end after CEO option exercises and the restricted 2025 award), not the ~3.5B I used. That lowers every enterprise-value component of my SOTP by ~11%. I also found my net cash was overstated: it is $27.4B net ($43.5B cash less $16.1B debt incl. leases), and the SpaceX stake carries at only ~$3B. Separately, I trimmed probability-weighted autonomy value from $550B to $520B because the NHTSA probe is now a sworn Special Order (response due Sept 30) over a real FMVSS design issue and the EU vote slipped to December at the earliest. The SOTP falls from $340 to ~$285, and a 120x P/E cross-check gives $260. The price is ~171x 2027E EPS ($2.17 confirmed), so fundamentals will not bind within 12 months. The stock trades on autonomy and AI narrative, and the sell-side median of $415 shows that. I therefore lower my median only modestly, from $360 to ~$352, rather than all the way toward the SOTP. Q2 deliveries and revenue were strong, H1 operating cash flow was up 84% and H1 FCF was roughly break-even, so the core is not collapsing. Scenarios: bear $220/27%, base $360/48%, bull $570/25%, mean ~$375. Ladder: lognormal with median $352 and sigma 0.49 (vs 46% realized vol, for binary regulatory and robotaxi events), with a slightly fattened lower tail (P(<223)=0.18). I agree with the supervisor on wide tails and lower merger odds. I disagree mildly on the thesis break: I keep $255 rather than $258 (immaterial). Research used about 6 extra queries and fetches. No options data and nothing under priors/ was used.
